### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3819afeca1307a2c1095ff4abe2eeaa6871d1b2a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e997e922bf2bf8d3f94c4f42087ca942c4c38b9f` — the merge of head `2cd098bdec6ff2b8849856fd9725bf971a7dcebf` into base `3819afeca1307a2c1095ff4abe2eeaa6871d1b2a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e997e922bf2bf8d3f94c4f42087ca942c4c38b9f && git checkout e997e922bf2bf8d3f94c4f42087ca942c4c38b9f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3819afeca1307a2c1095ff4abe2eeaa6871d1b2a 2cd098bdec6ff2b8849856fd9725bf971a7dcebf && git checkout -B drift-repro 3819afeca1307a2c1095ff4abe2eeaa6871d1b2a && git merge --no-ff 2cd098bdec6ff2b8849856fd9725bf971a7dcebf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3819afeca1307a2c1095ff4abe2eeaa6871d1b2a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：流程里“给字段赋值”的那一步，如果把日期字段的文字直接拿去计算，校验给出的报错现在说“计算这个值时流程会失败、停在这一步”，不再错说成“条件运行时”。
- 为什么做：赋值这一步根本没有条件，旧说法会让写流程的人找错地方。
- 出错会怎样：拦下来的写法、严重程度和修改建议都没变，只是报错文字换了；靠报错编号做自动处理的人需要认新编号。
- 要你做什么：不需要你做任何事，区域审完自己落地。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#5 · head `2cd098bdec6ff2b8849856fd9725bf971a7dcebf` · 2026-11-19T06:39Z

- **形态** — 5 files, +191/−22 (213 lines), all `packages/formula/src/**` plus one changeset. No `packages/spec/src` path. Base `81c09477`, main moved K=12 first-parent commits (< 15, no merge needed). `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35358`: not governed, under the 3000-line limit. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Fixes vs card #34660** — `flowValueEnvelopeDateTextIssue` now passes the new `value-run-may-fail` arm (`DateTextArm = DateArm | 'value-run-may-fail'`). The code is built as `date-text-{arithmetic,call}-${flowArm}`, so the envelope gets `date-text-arithmetic-value-run-may-fail` / `date-text-call-value-run-may-fail`. `dateArmFault` gives that arm its own clause ("when the value is computed … the flow stops at this step …") and returns before the condition sentence, so flattened conditions keep `-run-fails` / `-run-may-fail` text byte for byte. Both codes are in `ExpressionRefusalParams` (with the params of the code each splits from) and in `CODE_TABLE`. The `date-arithmetic` family never reaches an envelope, so it has no new arm. All three "Done when" items are met: value wording, ledger registration, and one verdict for both doors (via the shared entry; see deviations).
- **Clause-② no — agreed** — the accept set, grade (error), location, leading envelope sentence and fix hint are unchanged; only the code and the outcome sentence change on envelope sites. The changeset tells a consumer keyed to the old codes on an envelope to re-key. The dev found no consumer of these codes outside `packages/formula` beyond changelogs.
- **Changeset** — `@objectstack/formula` patch, read sentence by sentence against the diff: both envelope kinds, both example sources, the quoted old and new sentences (the new one matches `dateArmFault` verbatim), the two codes and their params, `ExprSchemaHint.flowValueEnvelope`, and the "Unchanged" list all match.
- **Pins** — `expression-refusal-codes.test.ts`: a PINS entry for each new code with its exact params and full message (the call pin carries the `shift` clause), and a 16th sweep schema (`flowValueEnvelope: true`, a date field) so the sweep's positive control reaches them. `validate-date-text-arithmetic.test.ts` moves the envelope cases to the new codes. The red leg is recorded at `240b77bf9c` (5 failed, then green 141/141).
- **门禁** — 68 check-runs on this head: 57 success, 11 skipped (path-filtered), 0 failure.
- **接受的偏差** — (1) The "lint and registerFlow keep one verdict" pin sits on the shared `validateExpression(..., { flowValueEnvelope: true })` entry that both doors call. Pinning through both callers would need test files in `lint` and `service-automation`, outside the fence. Both doors were measured once on built packages (PR Verification). Accepted. (2) The sweep grew from 15 to 16 schemas, with timing re-measured and recorded in the docblock (192–225 ms vs 186–267 ms), and the budget unchanged. Accepted.
- **范围外去向** — the `registerFlow` refusal header always explains template braces, whatever refusal sits under it (`service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts` ~:1047). This is pre-existing and misleading, but not a correctness, red-line or security issue, so it does not block. Route: ux-3 files its drafted card, nested under #34660.
- **落地条款** — not governed: ux-3 lands this head after this ACCEPT. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.
